primitives.name: Countable Union Closure Property
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2) Countable sets; the union of countably many countable sets is countable.
primitives.assumptions: Standard ZFC set theory framework; no additional cardinality axioms required.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when attempting to apply to uncountable unions, leading to cardinality paradoxes such as the power set of natural numbers being uncountable.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's discrete event space partitioning where each hypothesis corresponds to a countable set, enabling countable additivity of probability measures across disjoint event partitions. Also maps to GSE's finite-state machine transitions where each reachable state forms a countable set.
layer2.telemetry: Measurable via the Kolmogorov complexity of the enumeration algorithm for the union set; higher complexity indicates potential non-constructive membership.

primitives.name: Heine-Borel Compactness
primitives.verbatim_quote: the rational numbers are dense, every open set is a countable union of disjoint open intervals), the Heine-Borel theorem.
primitives.assumptions: Working within the standard Euclidean topology on R^n, assuming completeness and separability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces where closed bounded sets are not compact, causing convergence issues in functional analysis.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's predictive confidence regions which must be compact to guarantee frequentist coverage guarantees under sequential testing. Maps to GSE's state-transition systems where compact action spaces ensure existence of optimal policies via Brouwer fixed-point arguments.
layer2.telemetry: Monitored through the covering number of the parameter space; rapid growth signals potential overfitting or computational intractability.

primitives.name: Sequential Limit Algebra
primitives.verbatim_quote: (5) Least upper and greatest lower bounds (called suprema and infima) of sets of real numbers and real valued functions; limits, superior limits, and inferior limits of sequences of real numbers and real valued functions.
primitives.assumptions: Standard real analysis framework with the Archimedean property; working with monotone sequences or bounded sequences in complete metric spaces.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular at points of divergence where limsup and liminf differ, indicating lack of standard convergence; also fails for non-contractive iterative algorithms.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's sequential Bayesian updating where posterior distributions converge to point masses (limits) or remain diffuse (limsup/liminf separation). Maps to GSE's reinforcement learning value iteration where convergence to a fixed point represents steady-state policy evaluation.
layer2.telemetry: Measured by the variance of empirical averages; increasing variance suggests slow convergence or multiple attractors.
